views.name: player_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_api_id,
  date,
  overall_rating,
  potential,
  preferred_foot,
  attacking_work_rate,
  defensive_work_rate,
  crossing,
  finishing,
  heading_accuracy,
  short_passing,
  volleys,
  dribbling,
  curve,
  free_kick_accuracy,
  long_passing,
  ball_control,
  acceleration,
  sprint_speed,
  agility,
  reactions,
  balance,
  shot_power,
  jumping,
  stamina,
  strength,
  long_shots,
  aggression,
  interceptions,
  positioning,
  vision,
  penalties,
  marking,
  standing_tackle,
  sliding_tackle,
  gk_diving,
  gk_handling,
  gk_kicking,
  gk_positioning,
  gk_reflexes,
  -- rank of snapshot per player_api_id by date desc (1 = most recent)
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC, id DESC) AS attr_snapshot_rank
FROM Player_Attributes

params.description: Provides the latest (and ranked) attribute snapshot per player_api_id from Player_Attributes, allowing queries about a player's most recent physical and skill attributes and their snapshot ranking.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the most recent attribute values for a given player (attr_snapshot_rank = 1). | Compare recent and prior attribute snapshots for a player by using attr_snapshot_rank to pick ranks (e.g., rank 1 vs rank 2). | Filter players by a specific attribute threshold using the latest snapshot (join on player_api_id and attr_snapshot_rank = 1). | Compose player-level reports that need stable one-row-per-player-at-snapshot inputs (use attr_snapshot_rank to choose snapshot). | Build features for models that require the most recent numeric attributes for each player.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the Player_Attributes row (source: Player_Attributes.id) | player_fifa_api_id: external FIFA player id (source: Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id) | player_api_id: internal player id used to partition snapshots (source: Player_Attributes.player_api_id) | date: snapshot date string as stored in Player_Attributes.date (source: Player_Attributes.date) | overall_rating: overall rating numeric (source: Player_Attributes.overall_rating) | potential: potential rating numeric (source: Player_Attributes.potential) | params.metric: attr_snapshot_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC, id DESC) -- rank of snapshot per player_api_id; 1 is the most recent
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_core.player_api_id = player_latest_attributes.player_api_id — safe because player_latest_attributes exposes one row per (player_api_id, attr_snapshot_rank). If you restrict to attr_snapshot_rank = 1, the join is one-row-per-player and will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core via player_core.team_id (or similar) only after joining player_core; do not join player_latest_attributes directly to team_core unless you have ensured a one-to-one relationship (use player_core as the bridge). | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join player_latest_attributes to any table or view that is one-to-many per player_api_id (for example match events, match_lineup_players_unpivot, match_goal_result_flags, or other per-match/per-lineup tables) without either (a) filtering to a single snapshot rank per player (e.g., attr_snapshot_rank = 1) and/or (b) aggregating the one-to-many side first. Joining without aggregation will multiply this view's rows and effectively duplicate attribute values across the many-side rows. | composition note for comparing snapshots: to compute deltas across snapshots, self-join player_latest_attributes to itself on player_api_id with different attr_snapshot_rank values (e.g., rank = 1 vs rank = 2). This is safe because attr_snapshot_rank is unique per player_api_id. | when joining to team_latest_attributes (RANK): join on team identifier fields exposed by team_latest_attributes (e.g., team_core.team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id) only after joining player_core or another bridge that maps players to teams; both RANK views are one-row-per-entity-per-rank and will not multiply measures if you join at the entity rank level (e.g., both filtered to rank = 1). | planner hint: if you need per-match features that combine attributes and many match rows, aggregate the match side (e.g., counts/sums) before joining to player_latest_attributes to preserve measure correctness.

views.description: For each player (player_api_id and player_fifa_api_id), return the most recent Player_Attributes snapshot with its ratings and attributes. Useful to join a player's current/latest attributes to matches, teams, or player lists. | Use for: Join latest player attributes to Match lineups; List players with their current overall_rating/potential; Filter players by attribute thresholds (e.g., overall_rating) using the latest snapshot

views.name: match_lineup_players_unpivot

  id AS id,
  match_api_id AS match_api_id,
  date AS date,
  season AS season,
  league_id AS league_id,
  country_id AS country_id,

params.description: Unpivoted match lineup players: one row per match, side (home/away), and position index mapping to the player in that slot.
params.when_to_use: Get the player occupying a specific lineup slot for a match (e.g., who was home_player_3 in match X). | Filter or aggregate events by player across lineup positions (e.g., count matches where a given player appeared in any lineup slot). | Join roster/attribute data (player or team attributes) to matches at the player level for composition (e.g., combine with player_latest_attributes to get player age at match). | Build match-level player lists or compute per-match/per-side lineups and derive counts or distinct players.
params.output_schema: id: match primary key from Match.id (the view's identifier for the match row). | match_api_id: original match identifier from Match.match_api_id. | date: match date from Match.date. | season: season identifier from Match.season. | league_id: league identifier from Match.league_id. | country_id: country identifier from Match.country_id. | home_team_api_id: home team id from Match.home_team_api_id (note: always the home team id regardless of side column). | away_team_api_id: away team id from Match.away_team_api_id (note: always the away team id regardless of side column). | side: literal value 'home' or 'away' produced by the UNION branches (indicates whether the player came from the home_* or away_* columns). | position_index: integer 1..11 (or higher if source had more) indicating which numbered lineup slot this row represents; comes from the explicit constant in each SELECT. | player_api_id: player id taken from the corresponding horizontal column in Match (home_player_1, home_player_2, ..., away_player_1, ...).
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.date | Match.season | Match.league_id | Match.country_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.home_player_1 | Match.home_player_2 | Match.home_player_3 | Match.home_player_4 | Match.home_player_5 | Match.home_player_6 | Match.home_player_7 | Match.home_player_8 | Match.home_player_9 | Match.home_player_10 | Match.home_player_11 | Match.away_player_1 | Match.away_player_2 | Match.away_player_3 | Match.away_player_4 | Match.away_player_5 | Match.away_player_6 | Match.away_player_7 | Match.away_player_8 | Match.away_player_9 | Match.away_player_10 | Match.away_player_11
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated measures; it is a row-level reshape/unpivot. Derived columns are direct projections or literals: id = Match.id, match_api_id = Match.match_api_id, date = Match.date, season = Match.season, league_id = Match.league_id, country_id = Match.country_id, home_team_api_id = Match.home_team_api_id, away_team_api_id = Match.away_team_api_id, side = literal('home'|'away'), position_index = literal(1..11), player_api_id = respective Match.home_player_N or Match.away_player_N.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_latest_attributes on player_api_id = player_latest_attributes.player_api_id — safe because this view has at most one row per (match id, side, position_index) and player_latest_attributes is one-row-per-player (RANK), so player attributes will not duplicate lineup rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_api_id = player_core.player_api_id — safe for the same reason as above (player_core is NORM/one-row-per-player). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core or team_latest_attributes on home_team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id (or away_team_api_id accordingly) — safe because team_core is one-row-per-team; joining by team id will not multiply lineup rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_with_country on league_id = league_with_country.league_id — safe because league_with_country is one-row-per-league. | do NOT blindly join to match_goal_result_flags (AGG) or other aggregated-by-match views without considering aggregation keys: if match_goal_result_flags is one-row-per-match (aggregated), join on id = match_goal_result_flags.id is safe because it is one-row-per-match and will not duplicate lineup rows. However, if a sibling view is aggregated to multiple rows per match (e.g., per-goal, per-event), joining directly will multiply this view's rows and any derived counts. In that case you must either aggregate the many-side before joining (e.g., group to one row per match) or join using DISTINCT/EXISTS patterns. | do NOT join this view to one-to-many event tables (for example a goals/events table with multiple rows per match or per player) without re-aggregation because those joins will multiply lineup rows and any row-count based metrics. Instead, aggregate the event table to the same grain (match id, side, position_index or player_api_id) before joining. | Composition pattern examples: to compute how many matches a player appeared in during a season, aggregate this view grouping by player_api_id and season (COUNT(DISTINCT id) or COUNT(*) if one row per match-player is guaranteed). To enrich each lineup row with player attributes, perform a LEFT JOIN to player_latest_attributes on player_api_id; this preserves one row per (id,side,position_index).

views.description: Unpivot match lineup columns (home_player_1..11 and away_player_1..11) into one row per match-player participation with side and position index. Useful to join match events, compute appearances, or attach player attributes to each match participation. | Use for: Count appearances per player or per team; Join player attributes to each match participation; Find matches where a given player appeared (by player_api_id); Compute minutes/starting XI vs substitutes if substitute data available downstream

views.name: team_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  team_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  buildUpPlayDribbling,
  buildUpPlayDribblingClass,
  buildUpPlayPassing,
  buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  buildUpPlayPositioningClass,
  chanceCreationPassing,
  chanceCreationPassingClass,
  chanceCreationCrossing,
  chanceCreationCrossingClass,
  chanceCreationShooting,
  chanceCreationShootingClass,
  chanceCreationPositioningClass,
  defencePressure,
  defencePressureClass,
  defenceAggression,
  defenceAggressionClass,
  defenceTeamWidth,
  defenceTeamWidthClass,
  defenceDefenderLineClass,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_api_id ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC, id DESC) AS team_attr_snapshot_rank
FROM Team_Attributes

params.description: Provides the latest (most recent date) attribute snapshot per team (team_api_id) with a rank for each snapshot and the attribute fields from Team_Attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get the most recent attribute scores/classes for a team (e.g., scouting, team characteristic displays). | Filter teams to their latest snapshot before joining to match- or season-level data. | Compose into queries that need team-level attributes as point-in-time dimensions (join by team_api_id and optionally filter team_attr_snapshot_rank = 1). | Compare attribute changes over time by using team_attr_snapshot_rank to select Nth-latest snapshots per team.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the Team_Attributes row (Team_Attributes.id) | team_fifa_api_id: FIFA identifier for the team (Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id) | team_api_id: internal team identifier for the team (Team_Attributes.team_api_id) — the partition key used to determine the latest snapshot | date: snapshot date/time when these attributes applied (Team_Attributes.date) | buildUpPlaySpeed: numeric or coded score for build up play speed (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed) | buildUpPlaySpeedClass: categorical class for build up play speed (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass) | buildUpPlayDribbling: score for build up play dribbling (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribbling) | buildUpPlayDribblingClass: class for build up play dribbling (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribblingClass) | buildUpPlayPassing: score for build up play passing (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing) | buildUpPlayPassingClass: class for build up play passing (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassingClass) | buildUpPlayPositioningClass: positional/class bucket for build up play positioning (Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPositioningClass) | chanceCreationPassing: score for chance creation via passing (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing) | chanceCreationPassingClass: class for chance creation passing (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass) | chanceCreationCrossing: score for chance creation via crossing (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossing) | chanceCreationCrossingClass: class for chance creation crossing (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossingClass) | chanceCreationShooting: score for chance creation via shooting (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShooting) | chanceCreationShootingClass: class for chance creation shooting (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShootingClass) | chanceCreationPositioningClass: class for chance creation positioning (Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPositioningClass) | defencePressure: defensive pressure score (Team_Attributes.defencePressure) | defencePressureClass: defensive pressure class (Team_Attributes.defencePressureClass) | defenceAggression: defensive aggression score (Team_Attributes.defenceAggression) | defenceAggressionClass: defensive aggression class (Team_Attributes.defenceAggressionClass) | defenceTeamWidth: defensive team width score (Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidth) | defenceTeamWidthClass: defensive team width class (Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidthClass) | defenceDefenderLineClass: defender line class (Team_Attributes.defenceDefenderLineClass) | team_attr_snapshot_rank: integer rank (1 = newest) computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_api_id ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC, id DESC)
params.grounded_columns: Team_Attributes.id | Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id | Team_Attributes.team_api_id | Team_Attributes.date | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribbling | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribblingClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassingClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPositioningClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossing | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShooting | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShootingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPositioningClass | Team_Attributes.defencePressure | Team_Attributes.defencePressureClass | Team_Attributes.defenceAggression | Team_Attributes.defenceAggressionClass | Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidth | Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidthClass | Team_Attributes.defenceDefenderLineClass
params.metric: team_attr_snapshot_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Team_Attributes.team_api_id ORDER BY datetime(Team_Attributes.date) DESC, Team_Attributes.id DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core on team_core.team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is one row per (team_api_id, team_attr_snapshot_rank) and usually used with team_attr_snapshot_rank = 1 to be strictly one-row-per-team, so measures/attributes will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_with_country only when the join key is at team level (e.g., via team_core -> league linkage) and ensure the join path is one-to-one; avoid joining team_latest_attributes directly to league tables that are one-to-many without aggregation unless the join key is one-to-one for the specific snapshot. | do NOT join directly to match_lineup_players_unpivot, match_goal_result_flags, player_latest_attributes, or player_core (these are one-to-many relative to a team snapshot) without aggregating first — such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate the attribute values. Instead, aggregate the many-side (for example, compute counts or aggregates per team_api_id and match/date) and then join back on team_api_id (and date if needed). | when composing time-aware joins: if you need attributes as of a match date, restrict team_latest_attributes by team_attr_snapshot_rank = 1 after filtering Team_Attributes to snapshots with date <= match.date, or perform a greatest-n-per-group lookup keyed by team_api_id and <= match.date to avoid assigning a later snapshot to an earlier match. | when using team_attr_snapshot_rank > 1 to analyze historical deltas, treat each rank as a separate grain (rows are at team_api_id x team_attr_snapshot_rank), and only join dimension tables that are one-to-one with team_api_id or that are keyed to the snapshot id (Team_Attributes.id).

views.description: For each team (team_api_id), return the most recent Team_Attributes snapshot with numeric tactic/defence measures and class labels. Useful to join team strengths to matches by taking the nearest snapshot prior to the match date in downstream queries by filtering on date. | Use for: Attach team tactical attributes to match records; Compare team attributes across leagues or seasons; Filter teams by buildUpPlaySpeed or defence metrics

params.description: One-row-per-match summary containing match identifiers, basic match facts (teams, score, date, season, league), possession, and a set of bookmaker odds columns from the Match table.
params.when_to_use: Get basic match-level facts (teams, score, date, league) for a specific match or set of matches by id, match_api_id, date range, season, league, or team. | Join match-level facts and odds into downstream analyses (e.g., win/draw/lose label creation, linking to team or league attributes) without aggregating measures at this level. | Build further match-level metrics or labels (e.g., home_win_flag, goal_differential, implied probabilities from odds) by composing SQL on top of this view. | Filter or slice matches by season, league, country, stage, or date before joining to one-to-many datasets (lineups, events, players).

Match.season (season identifier string) | league_id: integer - Match.league_id (foreign key to league) | country_id: integer - Match.country_id (country identifier from Match) | stage: text/integer - Match.stage (stage/round of the match as stored) | home_team_api_id: integer - Match.home_team_api_id (foreign key to home team) | away_team_api_id: integer - Match.away_team_api_id (foreign key to away team) | home_team_goal: integer - Match.home_team_goal (goals scored by home team) | away_team_goal: integer - Match.away_team_goal (goals scored by away team) | possession: numeric/text - Match.possession (possession measure as recorded in Match table) | B365H: numeric - Match.B365H (Bet365 odds for home win) | B365D: numeric - Match.B365D (Bet365 odds for draw) | B365A: numeric - Match.B365A (Bet365 odds for away win) | BWH: numeric - Match.BWH (Bwin odds for home win) | BWD: numeric - Match.BWD (Bwin odds for draw) | BWA: numeric - Match.BWA (Bwin odds for away win) | IWH: numeric - Match.IWH (Interwetten home win odds) | IWD: numeric - Match.IWD (Interwetten draw odds) | IWA: numeric - Match.IWA (Interwetten away win odds) | LBH: numeric - Match.LBH (Ladbrokes home win odds) | LBD: numeric - Match.LBD (Ladbrokes draw odds) | LBA: numeric - Match.LBA (Ladbrokes away win odds) | PSH: numeric - Match.PSH (Pinnacle home win odds) | PSD: numeric - Match.PSD (Pinnacle draw odds) | PSA: numeric - Match.PSA (Pinnacle away win odds) | WHH: numeric - Match.WHH (William Hill home win odds) | WHD: numeric - Match.WHD (William Hill draw odds) | WHA: numeric - Match.WHA (William Hill away win odds) | SJH: numeric - Match.SJH (Stan James home win odds) | SJD: numeric - Match.SJD (Stan James draw odds) | SJA: numeric - Match.SJA (Stan James away win odds) | VCH: numeric - Match.VCH (VC odds home win) | VCD: numeric - Match.VCD (VC odds draw) | VCA: numeric - Match.VCA (VC odds away win) | GBH: numeric - Match.GBH (GameBooker home win odds) | GBD: numeric - Match.GBD (GameBooker draw odds) | GBA: numeric - Match.GBA (GameBooker away win odds) | BSH: numeric - Match.BSH (Betsson home win odds) | BSD: numeric - Match.BSD (Betsson draw odds) | BSA: numeric - Match.BSA (Betsson away win odds)

params.metric: home_team_goal = Match.home_team_goal (raw count of goals scored by home team) | away_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal (raw count of goals scored by away team) | goal_difference = (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) (derived metric; not present as a column but safe to compute in queries built on this view) | home_win_flag = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal > Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (derived binary flag computed by consumers) | draw_flag = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (derived) | away_win_flag = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal < Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (derived) | implied_probability_from_odds(provider_odds) = 1.0 / provider_odds (example derived metric; compute per odds column e.g., 1.0 / B365H). Note: no bookmaker-implied probabilities are precomputed in the view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core on team_core.team_api_id = home_team_api_id OR team_core.team_api_id = away_team_api_id — safe because this view is one row per Match.id; joining to team_core (one-row-per-team) will not duplicate match-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_with_country on league_with_country.id = league_id — safe because league_with_country is one-row-per-league; it will not duplicate match rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes or player_latest_attributes on matching team_api_id/player_api_id for enrichment when those views are one-row-per-entity (RANK views are typically one-row-per-team/player) — safe if the target view is guaranteed to be one-row-per-key. | unsafe joins (will duplicate measures) — do NOT directly join this match-level view to one-to-many tables/views such as match_lineup_players_unpivot (RESHAPE) or match_goal_result_flags (AGG may be one-row-per-match-event depending on definition) without re-aggregation: these are multi-row-per-match datasets (lineups or events) and will multiply match rows and any measure aggregated at match granularity. If you need per-player or per-event detail, join and then re-aggregate back to match-level (e.g., SUM/CNT/AVG) to avoid duplicating match-level measures. | safe composition pattern when combining with one-to-many: first aggregate the child table to one-row-per-match_id (e.g., SELECT match_id, COUNT(*) AS lineup_count FROM match_lineup_players_unpivot GROUP BY match_id) and then join that aggregated result to this view on Match.id = match_id; this preserves match-level cardinality and keeps measures correct. | key recommendations: treat this view as the match/grain owner (grain = Match.id). Any join that preserves the 1:1 relationship between Match.id and the joined entity (e.g., dimensions keyed by league_id, team_api_id, country_id) is safe. Any join that is 1:N from match to the other table requires aggregation of the N side before joining.

views.description: Canonical projection of core Match columns (one row per match) exposing key identifiers, dates, teams, scores and common betting odds normalized for analysis. Useful as a base relation for league/season trends and joins to teams/leagues. | Use for: League-level aggregates (goals per match, home advantage); Betting-odds analysis and calibration; Time series of matches per team or league

views.name: player_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_name,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player

params.description: Provides one row per player with stable identifiers and basic biographical attributes.
params.when_to_use: Look up a player's identifiers (id, player_api_id, player_fifa_api_id) and basic demographics (name, birthday, height, weight). | Join player identifying info into match-, team-, or event-level analyses as the player dimension. | Compose into aggregations that need to group or filter by player (e.g., per-player counts or metrics) while keeping player metadata separate from event facts.
params.output_schema: id: internal Player.id (primary key of the Player table) — surrogate/internal unique identifier for the player, grain is one row per id. | player_api_id: Player.player_api_id — an alternate API identifier for the player (may be external to this DB). | player_name: Player.player_name — full name string of the player as stored in Player. | player_fifa_api_id: Player.player_fifa_api_id — FIFA-specific external id for the player (nullable depending on source). | birthday: Player.birthday — date of birth of the player (nullable). | height: Player.height — player's height as stored in the Player table (nullable; units as in source). | weight: Player.weight — player's weight as stored in the Player table (nullable; units as in source).
params.grounded_columns: Player.id | Player.player_api_id | Player.player_name | Player.player_fifa_api_id | Player.birthday | Player.height | Player.weight
params.metric: No derived numeric aggregates are defined in this view; all output columns are direct column projections from the Player table. | If you need counts or rates per player, derive them by aggregating fact tables (e.g., match events) grouped by player_core.id or player_core.player_api_id.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core on team_core.some_player_key only when that key is one-to-one with player_core.id — safe because player_core is strictly one row per Player.id so joining to true dimension tables keyed by Player.id will not duplicate player rows. | Safe to join to match_basic_summary when using a many-to-one join direction from player_core -> facts only if you aggregate match_basic_summary first to one row per player (e.g., SUM/CNT grouped by player id). If you join directly to a match-level table without aggregation, the match rows will multiply player_core rows (not safe if you expect one row per player). | Do NOT join player_core directly to one-to-many event/detail tables (for example play-by-play, lineup entries, or goals) without aggregating the event table to player-level first — direct joins will produce multiple rows per player and will duplicate any computed measures coming from player_core if treated as measures. | When composing metrics, use player_core as the dimension (GROUP BY player_core.id) and derive measures from fact tables with explicit aggregation. Example safe composition: SELECT p.id, p.player_name, COUNT(m.match_id) AS matches_played FROM player_core p JOIN (SELECT player_id, match_id FROM match_lineup_players_unpivot GROUP BY player_id, match_id) m ON m.player_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.player_name; | Joining to sibling RANK or NORM views is safe only when those sibling views are also one-row-per-player (check their grain). In particular, do not assume rank or reshape views are 1:1 without verifying their declared grain.

views.description: Canonical projection of Player entity exposing identifying keys and demographic attributes. Use when joining player names and birthday/physical attributes to matches or attributes snapshots. | Use for: Map player_api_id to player_name for reports; Filter players by age (compute from birthday) when joined to match date

views.name: league_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  League.id AS id,
  League.country_id AS country_id,
  League.name AS name,
  Country.name AS country_name
FROM League
LEFT JOIN Country ON League.country_id = Country.id

params.description: Provides one row per League with its id, country_id, league name, and the associated country's name (if any).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic league attributes (id, name, country_id) and the human-readable country name for display or filtering. | Compose into analytics that need league-level dimensional data (e.g., join leagues to teams, matches, or aggregated metrics by league). | Filter or group queries by country_name while retaining league identifiers for joins to other entities.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the league, derived from League.id | country_id: foreign key referencing the country for the league, derived from League.country_id | name: league's name, derived from League.name | country_name: country display name for the league, derived from Country.name (nullable when no matching Country)
params.metric: id = League.id | country_id = League.country_id | name = League.name | country_name = Country.name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core on team_core.league_id = league_with_country.id — safe because league_with_country is one-row-per-league, so teams attached to a league will not duplicate league rows; any team-level measures must remain at team grain or be aggregated when producing league-level metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_summary on match_basic_summary.league_id = league_with_country.id — safe for adding match-level attributes as long as you intend to expand to match-grain. If you need league-level aggregates of matches, aggregate matches (e.g., COUNT(*) or SUM(...)) grouped by match_basic_summary.league_id before joining back to league_with_country to avoid duplicating league rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes on team_latest_attributes.league_id = league_with_country.id — safe for adding latest team attributes per team, but note this produces one row per team; to keep league-level cardinality, pre-aggregate team_latest_attributes to league level. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., match_lineup_players_unpivot, match_goal_result_flags, player_latest_attributes) without aggregation: such joins will multiply league_with_country rows because those sources are many-per-match, many-per-team, or many-per-player. Instead, aggregate those sources to league_id (or team_id then to league_id) first, producing one row per league, and then join — or perform joins at the child-grain and then re-aggregate. | safe join to country dimension: join to Country on league_with_country.country_id = Country.id is redundant (the view already left-joined Country) but is safe because Country is one-row-per-country; joining on country_id will not duplicate rows. | When composing metrics: treat the view as a pure dimensional (non-aggregated) one-row-per-league table. Any measures originating from many-row children must be defined as aggregates over those children grouped by league_id before joining to this view to preserve cardinality.

views.description: Denormalized league rows joined to their country name. One row per League.id with country metadata. Useful for reporting leagues by country and joining to matches aggregated by country. | Use for: List leagues along with country for filtering; Aggregate match counts by country via league join

views.name: team_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  team_long_name,
  team_short_name
FROM Team

params.description: Canonical one-row-per-team identifier and basic name mapping for the Team table, used as the stable core/team dimension for joins and lookups.
params.when_to_use: Lookup or report that needs a team's canonical id and common name identifiers (API id, FIFA id, long and short names). | Joining team descriptive attributes into match-, player-, or roster-level datasets as a dimension table. | Composing higher-level aggregates by joining on team id (e.g., team-level metrics, season summaries) where each team should appear once.
params.output_schema: id: surrogate PK for the team row, derives from Team.id | team_api_id: external API identifier for the team, derives from Team.team_api_id | team_fifa_api_id: FIFA external identifier for the team, derives from Team.team_fifa_api_id | team_long_name: full/team official long name, derives from Team.team_long_name | team_short_name: short/common team name, derives from Team.team_short_name
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics are produced by this view; all output columns are direct pass-throughs from base columns (id, team_api_id, team_fifa_api_id, team_long_name, team_short_name = Team.id, Team.team_api_id, Team.team_fifa_api_id, Team.team_long_name, Team.team_short_name respectively).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_summary on match_basic_summary.home_team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id OR match_basic_summary.away_team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id — safe because team_core is one-row-per-team (key = id / team_api_id) so these joins will not duplicate team_core rows; matches are the many side. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes on team_latest_attributes.team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id OR team_latest_attributes.id = team_core.id — safe because team_core is one-row-per-team and team_latest_attributes (RANK) is expected to be one-row-per-team (latest rank), so measures from team_core are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_core on player_core.team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id — not safe to do without aggregation on player_core first because player_core is many-per-team (players). If you need team-level player counts or summaries, aggregate player_core by team_api_id (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY player_core.team_api_id) before joining to team_core so team rows don't multiply. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_lineup_players_unpivot or player_latest_attributes without pre-aggregation is NOT safe because those views are many-to-one with team_core (multiple lineup/player rows per team). To compose correctly, either (a) aggregate the many-side to one row per team (e.g., SUM, COUNT, AVG grouped by team_api_id) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate results grouped by team_core.id to avoid duplicating team measures. | do NOT join team_core to any one-to-many view (e.g., match_goal_result_flags (AGG) if it is broken down per-event) expecting to preserve one-row-per-team semantics unless the other view has been reduced to one row per team. Always ensure the side being joined into team_core is aggregated to team_api_id or team id when you need to maintain team-level cardinality.

views.description: Canonical projection of Team entity exposing identifiers and display names. Useful for joining to matches and team attributes. | Use for: Resolve team_api_id to readable name in match reports; Filter teams by name or short code

views.name: match_goal_result_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  date,
  season,
  league_id,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal,
  (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) AS goal_difference,
  CASE WHEN home_team_goal > away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS home_win,
  CASE WHEN home_team_goal < away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS away_win,
  CASE WHEN home_team_goal = away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS draw
FROM Match

params.description: One-row-per-match flags and score measures indicating result (home/away/draw) and goal difference for matches.
params.when_to_use: Get match-level results (who won, goal counts, draw) for reporting or filtering. | Filter or group matches by outcome (home win / away win / draw) or goal difference. | Compose match-level aggregates (counts of home wins, average goal difference) by season/league/team. | Join match result flags to team/league metadata (team name, country) to produce human-readable reports. | Build time-series of match outcomes or compute team season summaries after appropriate aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the match row — derived directly from Match.id | match_api_id: external match identifier — derived directly from Match.match_api_id | date: match date/time — derived directly from Match.date | season: season identifier (string) for the match — derived directly from Match.season | league_id: foreign key to the league for the match — derived directly from Match.league_id | home_team_api_id: foreign key to the home team for the match — derived directly from Match.home_team_api_id | away_team_api_id: foreign key to the away team for the match — derived directly from Match.away_team_api_id | home_team_goal: integer goals scored by home team — derived directly from Match.home_team_goal | away_team_goal: integer goals scored by away team — derived directly from Match.away_team_goal | goal_difference: home_team_goal - away_team_goal (signed integer) — computed expression from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal | home_win: indicator (1/0) whether home_team_goal > away_team_goal — computed boolean-as-int from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal | away_win: indicator (1/0) whether home_team_goal < away_team_goal — computed boolean-as-int from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal | draw: indicator (1/0) whether home_team_goal = away_team_goal — computed boolean-as-int from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.date | Match.season | Match.league_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal
params.metric: goal_difference = Match.home_team_goal - Match.away_team_goal | home_win = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal > Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | away_win = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal < Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | draw = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_core (or team_latest_attributes) on match_home_team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id and/or match_away_team_api_id = team_core.team_api_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-match (unique by Match.id) and team_core is one-row-per-team, so the join is many-matches-to-one-team and will not duplicate match-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to league_with_country on league_id = league_with_country.league_id — safe because league_with_country is one-row-per-league and the view is one-row-per-match, so league attributes won't duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_summary on id = match_basic_summary.id or match_api_id = match_basic_summary.match_api_id — safe because match_basic_summary is normalized per-match (one row per match id) and will not multiply rows. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many/detail tables such as match_lineup_players_unpivot (which is one-to-many: each match has many players) because joining directly will duplicate this view's match-level measures; instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many table to one-row-per-match before joining (e.g., count of players per match), or | - join and then re-aggregate grouping by match id to recover match-level granularity. | when composing team-season aggregates (e.g., team wins in a season), aggregate this view after pivoting matches to the team grain (for example: UNION two rows per match mapping home_team_api_id with home_win and away_team_api_id with away_win) or compute separate aggregations for home and away then sum — do not join this view directly to a team-season table expecting one-row-per-team-season without grouping, because each match may relate to two teams and would need explicit transformation. | joining to player_core or match_lineup_players_unpivot: these are one-to-many relative to Match; avoid direct joins unless you first reduce the player-level data to match-level summaries (e.g., player counts, distinct player ids per match) to prevent multiplication of match measures.

views.description: One row per match with derived result flags indicating home_win, away_win, draw and goal_difference. Useful for aggregations of outcomes and computing home advantage metrics. | Use for: Compute counts of home/away wins and draws by team/season/league; Analyze goal difference distributions

views.name: match_team_goal_records
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS match_id,
  m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  'home' AS team_role,
  m.home_team_goal AS team_goal,
  m.season AS season,
  m.date AS date,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.country_id AS country_id
FROM Match m
UNION ALL
SELECT
  m.id AS match_id,
  m.away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  'away' AS team_role,
  m.away_team_goal AS team_goal,
  m.season AS season,
  m.date AS date,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.country_id AS country_id
FROM Match m
grain: one row per Match.id + team_api_id (one appearance)
views.description: One row per team appearance in a match with the goals that team scored and match context. Unpivots Match home/away goal columns into a canonical team appearance record.

views.name: team_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_api_id,
  team_long_name,
  team_short_name
FROM Team
views.description: Canonical team dimension with stable identifiers and display names (nullable). Exposes team_api_id and team_long_name/short_name for joins and presentation.

views.name: team_max_goals_per_team
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mtgr.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  MAX(mtgr.team_goal) AS team_max_goals,
  COUNT(*) AS appearances_count
FROM
  match_team_goal_records mtgr
WHERE
  mtgr.team_goal IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  mtgr.team_api_id
views.description: Per-team aggregate of the maximum goals scored in any single match appearance across the dataset. Uses match_team_goal_records to compute team_max_goals and exposes team identifiers for joins and further analysis.

views.name: matches_minimal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_api_id,
  league_id,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal
FROM Match
views.description: One row per match with only the columns needed for team-level win calculations and league association. Keeps raw goals and team ids so multiple derived aggregations can be computed later.

views.name: team_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  team_api_id,
  team_long_name,
  team_short_name,
  id
FROM team_core
views.description: Canonical team identity rows exposing stable team keys and human-readable names. Useful to left-join teams even when they have no matches or wins.
validated_on: Tell me top10 teams with the most wins across the league

views.name: team_wins_by_league
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  t.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN (m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id AND m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal) OR (m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal) THEN 1 END) AS wins
FROM Team t
LEFT JOIN Match m
  ON (m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id OR m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id)
GROUP BY
  m.league_id,
  t.team_api_id
views.description: Aggregated wins per team per league. Counts wins where team was home with home_team_goal > away_team_goal or away with away_team_goal > home_team_goal. Keeps zero-win teams via LEFT JOIN from team_identity when applied in the final query.

views.name: matches_basic_result_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_api_id,
  m.home_team_api_id,
  m.away_team_api_id,
  m.home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal,
  CASE
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 'home_win'
    WHEN m.home_team_goal < m.away_team_goal THEN 'away_win'
    WHEN m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal THEN 'draw'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS result
FROM Match m
WHERE m.home_team_api_id IS NOT NULL
  AND m.away_team_api_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per match with canonical home/away team ids and the match result (home_win/away_win/draw/unknown). Excludes matches missing both team ids. Keeps raw goal columns for flexibility.

views.name: team_match_win_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_api_id,
  m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  'home' AS role,
  CASE
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 1
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.home_team_goal < m.away_team_goal THEN 0
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal THEN 0
    ELSE NULL
  END AS win_flag,
  m.home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal
FROM Match m
WHERE m.home_team_api_id IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT
  m.match_api_id,
  m.away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  'away' AS role,
  CASE
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal < m.home_team_goal THEN 0
    WHEN m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal = m.home_team_goal THEN 0
    ELSE NULL
  END AS win_flag,
  m.home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal
FROM Match m
WHERE m.away_team_api_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Each match expanded into up to two team-level rows (one per participating team) with a win_flag indicating whether that team won the match. Keeps match and team roles (home/away) to allow role-based analyses.

views.name: matches_cleaned_played
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.season AS season,
  m.match_api_id AS match_api_id,
  m.date AS date,
  m.league_id AS league_id,
  m.home_team_api_id AS home_team_api_id,
  m.away_team_api_id AS away_team_api_id,
  m.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  m.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal
FROM Match AS m
WHERE m.home_team_api_id IS NOT NULL
  AND m.away_team_api_id IS NOT NULL
  AND m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
  AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
views.description: All played matches with non-null team ids and non-null final scores; keeps match-level fields needed for season-level aggregation and joins to teams/leagues/countries.

views.name: team_match_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  msp.id AS match_id,
  msp.season AS season,
  msp.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  1 AS is_home,
  msp.away_team_api_id AS opponent_team_api_id,
  msp.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  msp.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal,
  CASE
    WHEN msp.home_team_goal > msp.away_team_goal THEN 3
    WHEN msp.home_team_goal = msp.away_team_goal THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS points
FROM matches_cleaned_played msp

UNION ALL

SELECT
  msp.id AS match_id,
  msp.season AS season,
  msp.away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  0 AS is_home,
  msp.home_team_api_id AS opponent_team_api_id,
  msp.home_team_goal AS home_team_goal,
  msp.away_team_goal AS away_team_goal,
  CASE
    WHEN msp.away_team_goal > msp.home_team_goal THEN 3
    WHEN msp.away_team_goal = msp.home_team_goal THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS points
FROM matches_cleaned_played msp
grain: one row per team per Match (two rows per match: home team and away team)
views.description: Per-match, per-team points contribution derived from match result: produces one row per team per match indicating season and points earned (3/1/0). Useful for aggregating seasonal/team totals.

views.name: league_country_team_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  t.team_long_name AS team_long_name,
  t.team_short_name AS team_short_name,
  l.id AS league_id,
  l.name AS league_name,
  c.id AS country_id,
  c.name AS country_name
FROM Team t
LEFT JOIN League l ON l.country_id = t.id OR l.id IS NOT NULL
LEFT JOIN Country c ON c.id = l.country_id
grain: one row per Team x League x Country mapping where applicable (team_api_id keyed to team info; league and country exposed for joins)
views.description: Denormalized dimension joining Team, League, and Country to expose team identifiers and human-readable league and country names for reporting and grouping.
